artboards.title: The room — the row carries what the product knows
One document — a revision, not a sibling
Two refusals, drawn as first class
Built in the service, no surface

annotations.text:
SMART FILES IS NOT A FILE BROWSER, AND ITS BEST PROPERTIES ARE EXACTLY THE ONES A BROWSER HAS NOWHERE TO PUT.
It knows whether a document text is searchable and WHY NOT, in three named reasons. It knows a second upload under the same slug is a REVISION of one document, not a sibling. It knows who captured a file, when, from what kind of source and in what declared role - and REFUSES the write when any of that is missing. It knows what a document is placed against, not just which folder it sits in.
A browser shows name, size and date. The filing is the product.

THE DASHBOARDS "FILES" NAV ITEM IS A MOUNT POINT, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION.
smartcity-dashboards says so on itself: "This view mounts the serving Smart Files host with its own product top bar suppressed. It does not copy the browser."
So designing Files in dashboards would be designing a frame. The product is its own repo, its own database and its own serving process, and that is what these artboards are drawn against.

COVERAGE BEFORE RESULTS, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST MOVE ON THE CANVAS.
A search box over a corpus where some documents were never indexed is a box that LIES BY OMISSION. Three results can mean three matches, or it can mean twenty-eight documents were never searched, and every other product in this category cannot tell you which.
Smart Files can, because `search_text IS NULL` - never the empty string - is its one honest not-indexed value, and the three reasons are named on the row.
Here: 12 searched, 19 not, and SIX of the seven with no text layer are plan sets, which is exactly where a drainage easement would be drawn.

THREE REASONS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME THING.
content-type-not-indexable - a JSON meeting record was never eligible. Nothing failed.
no-text-layer - a scanned PDF. Something COULD read it, with OCR nobody has built.
extraction-failed - a corrupt PDF. Something tried and broke.
Different owners, different fixes, different answers to "can we find it". Collapsing them into "no results" is the defect, and it is the default everywhere else.

TWO UPLOADS, ONE DOCUMENT.
The second upload carried the same slug, so it became version 2 of this record rather than a second file beside it. entityId is unchanged, currentVersion increments, the response carries revision: true.
That is what makes a submittal identity STABLE ACROSS A REVISION CYCLE - the thing every plan review product in the category charges for - and a browser that drew two rows here would be describing the filing incorrectly.
Note also: only the CURRENT version is searched. A phrase in v1 removed in v2 is correctly not found.

FIVE KEYS, AND THE WRITE REFUSES WITHOUT THEM.
capturedBy, capturedAt, sourceKind, originalFilename, declaredRole. A missing or invalid key returns 400 rather than defaulting, and sourceKind is checked against a closed set of four so a caller cannot invent a category either.
originalFilename is kept deliberately: what the applicant called it ("Site Plan REV2 FINAL (2).pdf") is evidence. The slug is not.
All five are captured today and NO screen shows any of them.

BOTH REFUSALS ARE BETTER PRODUCT THAN THE THING THEY PREVENT, AND NEITHER IS DRAWN.
The read gate refuses anonymous and wrong-tenant IDENTICALLY, and the service is default-deny: an environment that has not configured its identities reads NOTHING, by design, rather than keeping the old defect as a silent default.
So the refusal should name the scope held and the scope required. A silent empty list is the alternative, and it teaches the caller that nothing is there.
Same shape on write: four of five provenance keys supplied means NOT FILED, because a provenance record with an invented field is worse than none.

WHAT IS BUILT AND WHAT IS REACHABLE ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.
Four capabilities landed in the service and have no surface, or have a surface that is chrome. Named rather than drawn as working, because a design that shows a capability as finished is how a capability stops being built.
The distinction that matters on this artboard is OWNER: three are surfacing work in this repo, one is a caller in smartcity-dashboards, and one needs a ruling. That is what decides who gets asked.

THE LINE THE PRODUCT ALREADY WROTE ABOUT ITSELF, KEPT VERBATIM.
On the People and access view: "Every grant, every link, every revoke, with a name and a time. This is the page a city attorney opens."
And on the access rail: "A share link is a row in this list with a name and a time, not a URL that exists off the record. Revoke sits at the same weight as the grant."
That is the right posture for a government filing system and it did not need redesigning. It needed the rest of the product brought up to it.
